message.text: `Comparison.misses()` flattens every external report in an external-only group, even though `Comparison.groups()` and the active restored comparison decision define that group as one defect and require each defect to contribute one miss.

evidence.snippet:
## From [2026-10-05-comparison-metrics.md](2026-10-05-comparison-metrics.md)

- Recall counts distinct valid groups. A reviewer gets credit only for its own report judged valid. Precision counts valid reports over valid, noise, and duplicate reports.
- An unadjudicated report is pending and enters neither metric.
- An external-only group whose valid reports all say `out-of-scope` stays outside Melian's recall denominator.
- An empty denominator gives 1, with the raw counts beside it. Reviewers aggregate by name and case-folded login, ignoring version.
- Earlier rounds stay in their statistics. A repeat on a second pull request is a candidate check. `melian compare stats` counts changesets as a stand-in, so two detached rounds of one pull request can still show as a candidate: a known gap, not policy.
- Withdrawing a finding leaves its history stored but removes it from that round's summaries.
- A group with conflicting miss reasons uses the first in-scope reason in site order, falling back to `out-of-scope`. Each defect contributes one miss. Titles that normalise to no letters or digits do not form repeat clusters.
- The drain counts each changeset once. At three or more comparisons, remaining debt keeps the drain due, including after a missed threshold. Local state cannot prove which backlog pull requests shipped or which live runs passed.

explanation.what: `Comparison.misses()` flattens every external report in an external-only group, even though `Comparison.groups()` and the active restored comparison decision define that group as one defect and require each defect to contribute one miss.
explanation.whatToDo: Build misses per external-only group, choose one representative using the established in-scope/site-order rule, and emit at most one case for that defect.
explanation.whyHere: When two reviewers report the same defect at the same site, the export emits two eval cases. That reviews and weights one defect twice, inflating cost and distorting miss-recall measurements; the design text was edited to describe per-finding output, but the active base decision says per-defect.

properties.failureScenario: Codex and Claude each report the same bug on lines 20-22, so `groups()` places their two valid `owned-missed` findings in one external-only group. Line 1023 flattens both reports and `compare misses` writes two cases. The measurement tool then runs and scores the same defect twice, although the active decision requires one miss per defect.

evidence.snippet:
`npm run eval:probing --workspace @melian-agent/evals` measures a level that probes, `trust-boundary`'s by default, against real models, for [issue #356](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/356). It runs on the harness `live.ts` uses: each review is `runGolden`'s, or `runRange`'s for a miss, so a review that is not reviewed, or whose level fell back to running without probes, gets no score. It reads the same settings `live.ts` reads, `MELIAN_EVAL_LIVE`, `MELIAN_EVAL_MODEL`, `MELIAN_EVAL_THINKING` and `MELIAN_EVAL_GOLDEN`, and these of its own:

- `MELIAN_EVAL_PROBE_ROUTES`: the combinations, separated by `;`. `label=planner>prober` runs a pair; `label=model` runs `deep` without probes on that model. Each model is read as core reads a model, so a model ID may hold `/` but not `>` or `;`.
- `MELIAN_EVAL_PROBE_LENSES`: the lenses that probe, separated by commas, `trust-boundary` by default. Each one's `deep` level probes, on the combination's planner and prober routes, for goldens and misses alike, and a miss's review runs every level of such a lens as its `deep`. Any other lens whose level already probes, by its committed `LENS.md` or because `lens` mode makes `trust-boundary` probe, follows the combination too: it runs on the planner's route, its probes run on the prober's, and the arm without probes drops them. Only a named lens gains a probe it does not declare. The run asks core's `Lens.probeRefusal()` whether each may probe, and exits 2 for one core refuses, such as `tests` until [issue #493](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/493) lands, a lens without probing wording, or a lens that takes a built-in's name without extending it. It also exits 2 for a name the base's policy does not load, and for a lens the tier of the review's `pull-request` stage does not run, since that review would score a prober that never ran. ## From [2026-10-05-comparison-as-a-capability.md](2026-10-05-comparison-as-a-capability.md)

- A comparison with external reviewers is a Melian capability, reached through `melian compare`, not a file an agent writes.
- An external finding has one shape. It names its reviewer, `codex`, `claude-code`, `coderabbit`, `copilot`, or `human`, with a version. It holds the file, line range, title, body, and the reviewer's severity. It keeps a stable source reference, the time posted, and whether its thread was resolved.
- A comparison holds, for one round, the external findings, Melian's, and the matches between them, in a document in the changeset's storage.
- Importers read a pull request's review threads through GitHub's GraphQL API, filtered by author login, with CodeRabbit's `coderabbitai[bot]` first. Others read a file: Codex's adversarial review JSON, or the external-finding shape for any other local reviewer.
- A `Decider` question may refine matching in milestone 4.
- `melian compare adjudicate` records valid, noise, or duplicate, a severity, and for a valid miss one reason: `owned-missed`, `no-owner`, `needs-execution`, or `out-of-scope`. It records too whether a golden is owed and for which lens, with the git author and time, as a dismissal is.
- `melian compare stats` gives recall and precision per reviewer, misses by reason, and repeat findings as candidate checks.
- `melian compare backlog` lists owed goldens, and `melian compare export` renders today's markdown record from the stored document.
- Every third comparison record is followed by a backlog pull request that ships at least two owed goldens, or every owed golden when fewer remain, and re-measures each new golden's lens with a live run of three passes, as the drain rule in docs/guidelines/evals.md sets out.
- A `needs-execution` miss is scope for the verifier, judged on whether it would have caught it, and for the tool manifest.

explanation.what: The export accepts every valid miss except `out-of-scope`, so it writes `owned-missed` and `no-owner` findings into a `MELIAN_EVAL_MISSES` file whose base contract says every entry is a `needs-execution` miss.
explanation.whatToDo: Export only findings whose effective miss reason is `needs-execution`, or introduce and document a separate input contract/tool mode for other miss reasons through an explicit amendment.
explanation.whyHere: The exported shape omits the adjudicated reason, so the measurement tool cannot distinguish these cases and treats them as its execution-dependent probing corpus. The new integration test explicitly feeds an `owned-missed` case into `Miss.load`, changing what the existing measurement counts without amending the base eval contract.

properties.failureScenario: The added integration test adjudicates a finding `{ verdict: "valid", reason: "owned-missed" }`, exports it, and loads it through `Miss.load`. Line 1026 includes that case but the output carries no reason. When supplied as `MELIAN_EVAL_MISSES`, the existing runner treats it as a `needs-execution` miss and measures the probing/default trust-boundary corpus against a defect that adjudication says an ordinary lens or check owns, producing a misleading corpus result.
